rules.title: State prohibition on local rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally compensated regulation of units owned by owners of ten or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.key_value: Statewide ban on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Voluntary, compensated local regulation limited to owners of ten or more units and units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts.
rules.conflict_note: State bar on local rent control; may preempt local rent control ordinances in MA cities.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent increase cap (blocked from 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC ruled in June 2026 that it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5% annual cap (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.review_note: Proponents say the defect is easily fixable and may re-file for 2028. Merged WBUR report (D059), which does not give the petition number.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can stop termination by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, by the answer day in an eviction case.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit; right to cure
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Notice to determine tenancy at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will ends with 3 months' written notice (or the rent interval or 30 days if longer and rent is paid more often than quarterly). For nonpayment, 14 days' notice to quit applies, and a tenant without a similar notice in the prior 12 months can cure by paying within 10 days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days for nonpayment; 10-day cure
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state an effective date.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancy must be at will (not a fixed-term lease)

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants who report violations or organize
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, or joining a tenants' union. Liability is 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages plus attorney's fees; a termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change in terms within six months is presumed a reprisal.
rules.key_value: 1-3 months' rent or actual damages; 6-month rebuttable presumption
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state an effective date.
rules.penalty: Damages of not less than one nor more than three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment: required state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment must be accompanied by a state form listing rental assistance programs, court rules and eviction restrictions, with a statement that the notice is not an eviction. Courts will not accept a nonpayment summary process filing without proof the form was delivered.
rules.key_value: State form must accompany nonpayment notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section

rules.title: Security deposit limit and handling
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account with a receipt and statement of condition, 5% annual interest (or the bank rate if lower), and be returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends less itemized lawful deductions.
rules.key_value: Cap of 1 month's rent; return within 30 days; 5% interest
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date of the cap not stated. The Aug. 1, 2025 amendment added agents and authorized regulations for a fee in lieu of a deposit.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable to vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit; treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees for certain violations.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges at lease start (no application fees by landlords)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord (or agent, from Aug 1, 2025) may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Application, screening and similar fees are not permitted.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit (max 1 month) and lock/key cost
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.effective_date_note: The limit on lessors is long-standing (secondary source: since the 1970s); the extension to agents took effect 2025-08-01.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable to vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.review_note: Application-fee reading comes from a secondary source (D054); licensed brokers are treated differently.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the broker pays
rules.requirement: A licensed broker may contract with either the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any broker fee must be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Amended text effective August 1, 2025 per 2025, 9, Sec. 136.

rules.title: Ban on discrimination against public assistance and housing subsidy recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against someone because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a program requirement. Landlords also may not refuse to rent or ask about protected characteristics such as race, sex, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.
rules.key_value: No discrimination against public assistance / housing subsidy recipients
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not give an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Subsection 7 excludes a single apartment in a two-family dwelling occupied by the owner.

unverifiable_exemptions: Subsection 7 does not apply to a single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling
Subsection 11 (children) has exemptions for small and owner-occupied dwellings

rules.title: S.2983 – An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. It was reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law; the page does not show operative text.
rules.key_value: pending ban on algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.interaction: New draft of S.994 and S.1016.

rules.title: H.5222 – An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending House bill on algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing. Reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to House Ways and Means. It is not law; the page does not show operative text.
rules.key_value: pending bill on algorithmic rent fixing
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

parsed.notes: Dropped c97 (254 C.M.R. 7 broker disclosure; licensing regulation, cited only in a secondary source). Merged S.2983 duplicates and the two failed rent-cap initiative records. Link-only D056 (803 CMR 5, CORI housing) not added: its text was not captured. Effective dates for long-standing G.L. provisions are not stated in the documents, so they are left null.
